scene1.title: Act 1: The "Academic Premiere" at Liyue Harbor Docks

content.text: Setting: Liyue Harbor Docks, high noon. Blazing sunlight beats down as crowds bustle to and fro. Yao Liqun has somehow procured a stack of wooden crates and piled them into a three‑tiered "lectern". Centered atop the lectern stands a hand‑written sign — *Teyvat Institute of Theoretical Physics · 48th Public Lecture · Free Admission · Opponents Please Bring Your Own Arguments · Those Who Mock Without Opposing Please Bring Your Own Sunflower Seeds*.

Liu Zhaolong stands beside the lectern holding up an even larger sign. Its text reads — *Everything she says is wrong. Do not call for guards, do not hurl vegetable scraps, do not alert the Millelith. If she has rambled for over ten minutes, contact the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor immediately.*
Tucked on the reverse side of the sign is smaller fine print: *Wangsheng contact details are on the back. Director Hu Tao says mention my name for a 10% discount.*

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Standing atop the stacked crates, holding a makeshift sky model cobbled together from raspberries, mint sprigs and a shard of fractured glaze, several chicken feathers stuck into its surface) Fellow citizens of Liyue! Travelers passing through! Pedestrians forced past by the burdens of daily life! Today I will demonstrate a revolutionary truth —

content.speaker: Random Passerby A
content.text: (Carrying a vegetable basket) Last time you claimed "Venti is fake, merely an air elemental manifestation".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Waving her hand) That theory has been disproven! Because Mister Venti bought me a drink. The wine was real, therefore he must be real.

content.speaker: Random Passerby A
content.text: Then you also once declared "Zhongli is fake, merely a rock spirit".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: That theory has likewise been overturned. Because Mister Zhongli treated me to tea.

content.speaker: Random Passerby A
content.text: When did Mister Zhongli ever treat you to tea?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: He did not do so directly. But he sat there drinking tea, and I watched him drink. By rough approximation, that counts as treating me.

content.speaker: Random Passerby A
content.text: ……(Silently steps three paces backward)

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Writing inside his notebook) Entry No.43: Yao Liqun’s standard of proof is "whether someone bought her alcohol or indirectly treated her to tea".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: But the sky is different! The sky has never bought me wine! Never treated me to tea! It has not even handed me a plain cup of boiled water! That is extremely suspicious!

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: (Squeezing out from the crowd, clutching half a skewer of grilled bird eggs) Traveler! It’s that eccentric scholar! Last time she said "Paimon is the biggest counter‑example to the emergency‑food theory, because emergency food cannot talk!"

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: (Steps forward behind Paimon) ……

options.text: "What she said back then actually made a fair bit of sense."
"Let’s hear what she has to say."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: What did you just say?!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: ……Nothing.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: You always do this! Hiding half of what you mean! Back in Inazuma you said "The Raiden Shogun is actually quite reasonable", and then she nearly struck us down with lightning!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: That was different.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: How was it different?!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Back then I was wrong. This time I said nothing.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: But you did speak! Paimon heard you!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: You misheard.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Paimon didn’t mishear!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: You misheard.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Traveler, you’ve caught Yao Liqun’s madness. You’re starting to argue in circles too.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Eyes lock onto Paimon) Ah! Paimon! Perfect timing! You are Teyvat’s sole flying being!

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Paimon isn’t some being! Paimon is Paimon!

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Then what are you?

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: I’m…… I’m Paimon!

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: That is circular reasoning. You have not answered the question.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: You’re the one using circular reasoning! Your whole household uses circular reasoning!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Jots in notebook) Entry 43 Addendum 1: When logically outmatched, Paimon raises her volume.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Very well, Paimon, let me rephrase — what is the highest place you have ever flown to?

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Uh…… The Jade Chamber?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: How tall is the Jade Chamber?

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Really tall.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Precisely how tall?

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Extremely tall.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Have you flown high enough to touch the sky?

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: (Freezes) ……No.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Spreads arms toward the crowd) You all heard that! Teyvat’s only flying life‑form cannot reach the sky! It is not that the sky is too high — it is that the sky avoids you!

content.speaker: Random Passerby B
content.text: How can a sky avoid people?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Have you ever chased a cat? When a cat does not wish to be caught, you shall never catch it. The sky is just the same. Look up, and there it is. Fly upward, and it remains out ahead. You can never draw near to it.

content.speaker: Random Passerby B
content.text: That is merely because the sky is extremely far away!

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: "Extremely far" — how far is that exactly?

content.speaker: Random Passerby B
content.text: ……Really far?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: You too are trapped in circular reasoning! Every single one of you! This is the sky’s conspiracy! It makes us explain "far" with "far", explain "high" with "high"! It is a linguistic prison!

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: (Pops out of the crowd holding Wangsheng Funeral Parlor flyers) Whoa there scholar! Last time you claimed "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is Liyue’s largest underground intelligence agency", I’ve been thinking about it —

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: That was my Thesis No.7, it has already been disproven.

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: Disproven by what?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Your intelligence work is abysmal. I once asked you "Where does The Heavenly Principles reside?" and you replied "We have no clue". A genuine intelligence agency would at least fabricate a fake address.

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: ……Fair point. Want to sign up for our membership? Discounts for your after‑life services.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: I’ll pass for now, thank you. What I require is special‑purpose research funding for sky‑related studies.

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: Then you ought to seek out Ningguang. Though she once said "If I ever see Yao Liqun again, hurl her off the Jade Chamber".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: She said "her". I am female.

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: When Ningguang said "her", her tone carried far more weight.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: ……That must mean she holds me in high academic regard.

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: Her exact words were: "If that madwoman dares step near the Jade Chamber once more, I shall let her experience a genuine high‑altitude fall experiment."

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Eyes light up) A high‑altitude fall experiment! Ningguang understands my research!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Notebook update) Entry43 Addendum 2: Yao Liqun interprets every threat as an academic invitation.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Stands upright again, lifting up her sky‑model) Everyone! I shall now perform a live demonstration!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Looks upward) Qun, your last live demonstration blew up half the harbor docks.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: That was an accident. Back then I researched "Elemental power is in essence emotion". My oversight was failing to account for the fact that Liyue fishermen’s dominant emotion was "wanting to throw us into the sea".

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: You told one fisherman "Your fishing net looks like it rolled out of Fontaine Research Institute’s trash bin."

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Objective observation. Besides, he later admitted the net was imported from Fontaine.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: He said it was imported from Fontaine, not that it rolled out of their garbage.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Those two statements are not mutually exclusive.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Sighs) Entry43 Addendum3: To Yao Liqun, "not contradictory" equals "factually correct".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Holds the sky‑model high) Observe all! This construct represents Teyvat’s sky! Raspberries stand for cloud banks, mint sprigs stand for wind, glaze shard stands for the sun, and chicken feathers represent — (pauses) chicken feathers represent something I haven’t worked out yet, but that detail is unimportant!

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: What do the chicken feathers stand for exactly?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: They represent the unknown. Recognizing unknown variables is paramount for scholarly pursuit.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Why use chicken feathers for that, though?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Because chicken feathers were all I had on hand.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Why are you carrying chicken feathers around?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Yesterday I ran experiments on whether birds’ maximum flight altitude is affected by my sky‑hypothesis. I caught a chicken for testing purposes.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Chickens cannot fly!

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: That is precisely my discovery! Chickens cannot fly, yet they possess feathers. This proves feathers and flight hold no inherent necessary connection. By analogy: the sky and "objective reality" might also share no necessary connection!

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Traveler, Paimon’s head hurts.

options.text: "She is using a chicken as evidence that the sky is fake."
"There is actually a tiny grain of sense in her logic."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Can that really count as proof?

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: No. But she is trying.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: You almost said "a tiny grain of sense" just now, didn’t you?!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: I said no such thing.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Your lips moved! Paimon saw it!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: I was chewing sunflower seeds.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: You have no seeds in your hands!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: ……I finished them already.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Traveler!!!

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Now behold, I shall demonstrate the operational mechanism of the sky with this model! (Holds the model over her head and spins in circles) When I rotate this model — do you perceive the model spinning, or do you perceive yourselves spinning?

content.speaker: Random Passerby C
content.text: You are the one spinning.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Correct! But suppose you could not see my feet turning. If you only looked at the floating model itself?

content.speaker: Random Passerby C
content.text: ……Then I would believe the model spins on its own accord.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: That is the truth of our sky! We watch the sky turn, yet we cannot see what lies beneath it. We cannot see outside our world. We cannot see the entity that turns the sky!
Complete silence falls across the crowd for three full seconds.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Writes quickly) Entry43 Addendum4: For the first time, Yao Liqun’s argument rendered onlookers speechless. Worth recording.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: (Quiet whisper) Traveler…… what she just said kind of makes sense?

options.text: "Every individual line she speaks sounds reasonable. Spend three days with her, and you realize her reasoning loops in endless circles."
"Stop thinking about it. Everything she says is wrong."
"Do you want to hear more of her reasoning?"

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: "Circles" what circles?

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: She starts with her conclusion "the sky is fake", then hunts for supporting evidence. When evidence cannot be found, she declares "the lack of evidence itself serves as evidence".

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……That’s just cheating at logic!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: It is. But she argues with such total sincerity you feel bad calling her out on it.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Traveler, were you just praising her?!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: I was merely stating objective observation.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Your mouth corners twitched! You were holding back laughter!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: ……Still chewing those imaginary sunflower seeds.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: There you go again with the sunflower‑seed excuse! You don’t hold any!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: ……I finished them all.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: You gave that exact same answer earlier!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Because it remains true.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Aaaaah‑‑‑‑! (Crouches down clutching her head)

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Leaps down off the crates, nearly tripping; Liu Zhaolong catches her arm) Thanks. Everyone! Today’s lecture concludes here! Same time, same place tomorrow, I shall deliver our 49th public lecture. The title will be —

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Interjects) "On Why Yao Liqun Should Be Banned From Public Speaking".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Incorrect. Title: *The Sky‑Hypothesis and Deconstruction of Teyvat’s Social Structures — Also Touching Upon Why Ningguang Dares Not Let Me Enter the Jade Chamber*.

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: I think Ningguang’s stance is "does not wish to", not "dares not".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: "Does not wish to" is merely polite phrasing for "dares not"! Basic linguistics!

content.speaker: Hu Tao
content.text: ……Alright, you win this argument.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Suddenly remembers something) Oh right, Liu Zhaolong, make a note — how many attendees listened to today’s lecture?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Flips through notebook) From what I observed, full‑duration listeners are: myself, Paimon, the Traveler, Hu Tao, plus Passerby A with the vegetable basket.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Where is Passerby A now?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Left when you started talking about chickens having feathers despite being flightless.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: ……He still heard two‑thirds of the presentation. That counts as progress. Better turnout than last session.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Last time the audience was only me plus one stray dog.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Whatever happened to that dog?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: It followed us for three city blocks, then bolted the instant you proclaimed "the sky is fake".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: ……That dog was intelligent. It understood my thesis.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Writes) Entry43 Addendum5: Yao Liqun interprets a dog running away as proof the dog comprehended her arguments.

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: (Steps forward) You intend to lecture again tomorrow?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Of course! Scholarly inquiry cannot halt!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: How long have you pursued this research?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Ever since the first time I looked upward toward the sky.

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: How many years ago was that?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Pauses to think) ……I cannot recall. But my very first research notebook opens with the line: "The sky might be fake. Commencing observations today."

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Do you still possess that first notebook?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Yes. But its pages are filled with doodles of slimes.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Why all the slime drawings?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Back then I investigated whether slime elasticity correlates with the curvature of the sky.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Was there any correlation?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: None whatsoever. But I spent three months eliminating that possibility.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Three whole months?!

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: This is how research functions. You must first try to prove a connection exists before you can argue there is none. If you simply assert "there is no connection", others demand: "How can you be certain?". Therefore you invest three months attempting to validate the hypothesis, then announce: "This hypothesis is incorrect."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Didn’t those three months go completely to waste?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Not wasted at all! Those three months yielded the firm conclusion: "Slime elasticity bears no relation to sky curvature." A conclusion is valuable progress in itself.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Traveler, every point she makes sounds reasonable, yet something still feels fundamentally off.

options.text: "That is Yao Liqun’s peculiar danger. Every isolated sentence sounds sensible, yet strung together they dissolve into total confusion."
"If you feel that way, you are starting to understand her mindset."
"Quit over‑thinking this. Let’s go grab food."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Paimon feels like her brain is about to explode.

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Then stop dwelling on it.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: You’re right. Let’s find something to eat.

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Very well.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Wait‑‑ you almost said "you’re starting to understand her" just now, didn’t you? Paimon saw you hesitate!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: No I didn’t. I was thinking about what meal we should pick.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: "Thinking about food" is your go‑to excuse every single time!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Because food genuinely matters.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Ugh, you win this round.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Closes his notebook) Qun, we ought to depart. You have to collect your medicine from Bubu Pharmacy this afternoon.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: What medicine?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Sedative‑calming tonics.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: I require no calming tonics. My mind is perfectly lucid.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: What hour did you finally sleep last night?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: I never slept. I stayed up composing my research paper.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Paper title?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: *On the Relationship Between Sleep and the Sky‑Hypothesis — If the sky is fake, then could dreams also be fake?*

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Silent three‑second pause) ……So you skipped sleep in order to research whether dreams are fake?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Precisely. If dreams are fake, sleeping serves no purpose. If dreams are real, sleeping wastes valuable research hours. Therefore, whether dreams are real or fake, I logically ought not to sleep at all.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Silence) ……Qun, your reasoning holds. But we are still picking up that medicine.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: Why must I take it?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Doctor Baizhu warned that if you avoid collecting your medicine any longer, he will come down personally to these docks and announce in front of every onlooker: "Yao Liqun, your mind is not broken. You merely require sleep."

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Brief pause) ……Doctor Baizhu truly comprehends my work.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: His exact wording was "your mind is not broken".

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: "Not broken" is itself the greatest problem! If my mind functions normally, why do I perceive a world different from everyone else’s?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: That is simply sleep deprivation speaking.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: And you all sleep well — does that guarantee your perception of reality is genuine?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: ……Qun, let’s head over to Bubu Pharmacy.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: You are evading my philosophical question.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: I am. Because I also slept very poorly last night.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Liu Zhaolong couldn’t sleep either?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Last night she kept reciting her paper aloud until three in the morning. My lodging is right next‑door, and the walls are paper‑thin.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: What was she chanting?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: "The sky is fake, the sky is fake, the sky is fake, yet my paper is real, therefore the sky must be fake."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……That counts as an academic paper?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: That is only her concluding paragraph. There were three thousand preceding words of argumentation.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Three thousand words?!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: I listened through the wall. The first two thousand words discussed slime elasticity. The final thousand expounded on the symbolic meaning of chicken feathers.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……How did she arrive at that final conclusion from those premises?!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Her logic: "Slimes are elastic, therefore the sky can curve. Chicken feathers drift on air, therefore the sky can move. Ergo: the sky is fake."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: That…… that hardly qualifies as valid reasoning!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: It does not. But she delivers it at the top of her lungs.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Already ten paces away, shouting back over her shoulder) Liu Zhaolong, hurry up! I’ve conceived a brand‑new question to ponder en‑route to Bubu Pharmacy!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: What question?

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: If the sky is fake — is even the name "Bubu Pharmacy" itself fake?!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Turns toward Traveler & Paimon) And this is my everyday reality.

options.text: "Why don’t you simply run away from all this?"
"You could choose to leave her to her own devices."
"You have a great deal of patience."

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Falls quiet for a moment) Because once, she got something right.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: What statement was that?!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: She said: "Everyone across Teyvat pretends to be sane. Only I openly admit my own madness." Then she looked straight to me and added: "And you are the sole person who makes no pretense of normality."

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: I told her "I’m not mad". She replied: "You may not be mad, yet you choose to accompany a madwoman researching the sky. That in itself is already abnormal." (Chuckles softly) After thinking it through, I realized she had a fair point.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: So you choose this life of your own free will?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: I want to witness for myself: can she genuinely prove the sky is fake?

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: What would happen if she succeeds?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Then I shall stand beside her and accept whatever wrath The Heavenly Principles unleash upon us.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: And if she never succeeds?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Then I shall keep accompanying her research.

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: ……You two both carry more than a touch of madness.

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Smiles) Yes. But among Teyvat’s inhabitants, when madmen stick together, none among them are truly mad.

(A distant shout drifts over from Yao Liqun: "Liu Zhaolong! Another new thought! If the sky is fake — then is even the word "sky" fake? If words themselves are fake, is my statement "the sky is fake" also fake? Then have I said absolutely nothing at all?!")

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: (Rises to his feet) Coming!

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: That question she just yelled…… almost sounds proper philosophy?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: She spawns questions like this every single morning. My usual countermeasure is to shove breakfast into her mouth.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Does that trick actually work?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: It works perfectly. She stops rambling once food fills her mouth.

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: What food does she prefer?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Slime Condensate over steamed rice.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……What?!

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Just joking. Her real favorite is grilled fish. Though when finished eating, she arranges all the fish‑bones into curved sky‑shapes.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……And then what happens?

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: Then she declares: "See how these fish‑bones curve? Therefore the sky itself must curve!"

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: She always manages to dig up new pieces of "evidence".

content.speaker: Liu Zhaolong
content.text: That is Yao Liqun for you. You can never predict what absurd piece of evidence she will pull out next.
(Liu Zhaolong turns and hurries to catch up with Yao Liqun. Traveler and Paimon remain standing alone upon the harbor docks.)

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: Traveler, should we follow them to watch what unfolds?

options.text: "No. We have other business to attend to."
"Sure. I want to hear what she will lecture about tomorrow."
"Let’s eat first. We can decide afterwards."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: "Other business"? What sort of business?

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: "Go over to Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and find Zhongli. I want to ask him one question."

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: What question are you going to ask?

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: "Do you think there is even the remotest possibility Yao Liqun’s claims hold truth?"

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: ……Have you also caught her madness?!

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Pure curiosity, nothing more.
(Traveler tilts their head upward toward the heavens. The sky glows bright blue. Clouds drift. Shadows shift and slide across the ground.)

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: ……Clouds drift one way, shadows drift another. Their directions seem slightly mis‑aligned.

content.speaker: Paimon
content.text: So what of that?

content.speaker: Traveler
content.text: Nothing at all. Come on, let us depart.

(The pair walk away from the docks. Only the large lecture‑sign remains behind: *Teyvat Institute of Theoretical Physics · 48th Public Lecture*. Beneath the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor contact info on its reverse side, new handwritten characters appear in Yao Liqun’s handwriting: "If the sky is fake, then this sign is fake as well. But since you can read these words, this sign must at least have existed once. Does something that once existed count as real? — Yao Liqun, written after Lecture #48.")
——End of Act 1——
Post‑credits Easter Egg (Exclusive to Act 1)
Setting: Liyue Harbor Docks, deep night. Yao Liqun sneaks back alone, standing in front of her old wooden sign, brush held in‑hand.

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Stares at the writing on the board) ……"Does something that once existed count as real?"

(She ponders for a short moment, then scribbles another line underneath: "If yes, then the sky also once existed. If no, then my research paper cannot count as real. Therefore my paper must count as real, which forces the sky not to count as real.")

content.speaker: Yao Liqun
content.text: (Nods contentedly, turns to leave. Takes three steps, wheels back around and appends one final line: "Entire argument independently formulated by Yao Liqun. Liu Zhaolong is credited for grinding ink. Though he never actually ground ink, merely stood nearby. Moral support still qualifies as support.")
(She departs. Moonlight washes over the wooden sign, making its inked words faintly glow in the dark.)
